name: Protests against the Damascus blood libel
description: American Jews held their first coordinated public protests on behalf of Jews abroad, after the arrest and torture of Damascus Jews accused of ritual murder.

name: Abraham Rice takes the Baltimore pulpit
description: The first ordained rabbi to serve an American congregation.

name: Organ installed at Beth Elohim
description: Installation of an organ in the new Beth Elohim synagogue, and Poznanski's reforms, led traditionalists to secede and form Shearit Israel.

name: B'nai B'rith founded
description: Twelve German Jewish immigrants founded the Independent Order of B'nai B'rith.

name: Isaac Mayer Wise arrives in America
description: Wise arrived in New York and soon took the pulpit of Beth El in Albany.

name: First High Holy Day services in San Francisco
description: Gold Rush migrants gathered for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur services, the beginnings of organized Jewish life on the Pacific coast.

name: Rosh Hashanah confrontation at Beth El, Albany
description: After Wise's dismissal, a scuffle broke out on Rosh Hashanah; his supporters formed Anshe Emeth.

name: Leeser's English Bible published
description: The first complete Jewish translation of the Hebrew Bible into English published in America.

name: Judah Touro's bequests
description: Touro's will distributed his fortune among congregations, hospitals and charities in many cities, Jewish and Christian.

name: Cleveland Conference
description: Rabbinical conference convened by Wise in search of a union of American congregations; its platform was attacked from both the traditionalist and radical Reform sides.

name: Minhag America published
description: Wise's prayer book for American congregations.

name: Protests over the Mortara affair
description: Mass meetings protested the abduction of Edgardo Mortara in Bologna and led directly to the founding of the Board of Delegates of American Israelites (1859).

name: First rabbi opens the House of Representatives
description: Morris J. Raphall delivered the opening prayer in the U.S. House.

name: Einhorn flees Baltimore
description: Threatened by pro-secession mobs for his antislavery preaching, David Einhorn left Baltimore for Philadelphia.

name: First Jewish military chaplain commissioned
description: After lobbying by the Board of Delegates, Congress amended the chaplaincy law in July 1862; Jacob Frankel was commissioned as a hospital chaplain that September.

name: General Orders No. 11
description: Ulysses S. Grant expelled 'Jews as a class' from his military department. Paducah's Jews were driven out; after Cesar Kaskel's appeal, Lincoln had the order revoked in January 1863.

name: Maimonides College opens
description: First American rabbinical seminary.

name: Philadelphia Rabbinical Conference
description: Conference of Reform rabbis, led by Einhorn and Samuel Hirsch, that adopted a set of radical Reform principles.

name: Plum Street Temple dedicated
description: B'nai Yeshurun dedicated its Moorish Revival temple, a statement of the confidence of Cincinnati Jewry and of Wise's Reform movement.

name: Temple Emanu-El consecrated on Fifth Avenue
description: Emanu-El moved uptown to a Moorish Revival temple at Fifth Avenue and 43rd Street, following its members' move north.

name: Burials banned in lower Manhattan
description: A city ordinance forbidding burials below 86th Street closed the 21st Street cemetery and pushed congregations to new grounds in Cypress Hills.

name: Louis Sloss marries Sarah Greenebaum
description: The first marriage in the Sloss-Gerstle family network, celebrated in Philadelphia before the couple settled in California.

name: Sonora Hebrew Cemetery founded
description: The first Jewish burial ground in the Gold Rush mining region.
